catalog_title: Remote Sensing Indices and Spectral Metrics Catalog
description: Structured catalog of verified optical and radar spectral indices with exact formulas, parameters, mathematical ranges, and scientific citations.

provenance.note: Formulas represent canonical peer-reviewed publications. Thresholds are context-dependent and never universal.

mathematical_range.conditions: Non-negative surface reflectance inputs and non-zero denominator.

typical_observed_range.context: Water typically < 0; bare soil ~ 0.05 - 0.2; dense green canopy ~ 0.6 - 0.85

interpretation.caution: NDVI=0.65 does NOT equal 65% vegetation cover. FVC or leaf area requires calibrated empirical models.

limitations: Soil background brightness influences sparse canopy values
Saturation occurs in dense vegetation (LAI > 3-4)
Atmospheric aerosols and cloud shadows alter reflectance
science_references: Rouse, J. W., et al. (1974). Monitoring the vernal advancement and retrogradation of natural vegetation. NASA/GSFC Final Report, 371 p.

indices.formula: G * (NIR - RED) / (NIR + C1 * RED - C2 * BLUE + L)

mathematical_range.conditions: Denominator is not constrained to NIR + RED; range is not strictly [-1, 1].

interpretation.caution: Requires valid blue reflectance; residual blue noise or cloud contamination causes high distortion.

limitations: Requires reliable blue band reflectance (easily corrupted by aerosols)
Denominator can approach zero in dark or shadow pixels causing extreme values
science_references: Huete, A., et al. (2002). Overview of the radiometric and biophysical performance of the MODIS vegetation indices. Remote Sensing of Environment, 83(1-2), 195-213.

indices.name_ar: مؤشر الغطاء النباتي المحسن ثنائي النطاق

mathematical_range.conditions: Omits blue band to avoid atmospheric noise.

typical_observed_range.context: Consistent with 3-band EVI in unpolluted conditions

limitations: Slightly higher sensitivity to sub-pixel clouds than 3-band EVI
science_references: Jiang, Z., et al. (2008). Development of a two-band enhanced vegetation index without a blue band. Remote Sensing of Environment, 112(10), 3833-3845.

mathematical_range.conditions: L=0.5 default; L=1 for low density, L=0.25 for high density

limitations: Requires tuning L factor when vegetation density is extreme
science_references: Huete, A. R. (1988). A soil-adjusted vegetation index (SAVI). Remote Sensing of Environment, 25(3), 295-309.

indices.name_ar: مؤشر الغطاء النباتي المعدل للتربة المطور

mathematical_range.conditions: Term under radical must be non-negative

limitations: Radical expression must be protected against negative values in noisy pixels
science_references: Qi, J., et al. (1994). A modified soil adjusted vegetation index. Remote Sensing of Environment, 48(2), 119-126.

indices.name_en: Normalized Difference Water Index (McFeeters - Surface Water)

typical_observed_range.context: Open water > 0 (or empirically calibrated zero-line); vegetation and soil < 0

interpretation.caution: DO NOT confuse with Gao 1996 (NIR-SWIR) which measures vegetation canopy moisture. Built-up land may yield positive false water pixels in McFeeters NDWI.

limitations: Confounds open water with asphalt, urban shadows, and dark impervious surfaces
Requires masking of topographic shadows in hilly terrain
science_references: McFeeters, S. K. (1996). The use of the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) in the delineation of open water features. International Journal of Remote Sensing, 17(7), 1425-1432.

indices.name_en: Normalized Difference Water Index (Gao - Canopy Moisture)
indices.name_ar: مؤشر المحتوى المائي للغطاء النباتي (جاو / NDMI)

required_inputs.description: SWIR band ~1.24 µm (Gao 1996 original) or ~1.6 µm (standard satellite adaptation / NDMI)

typical_observed_range.context: High canopy water content: 0.2 - 0.5; dry/stressed canopy < 0

interpretation.caution: Measures liquid water in plant canopies, NOT open surface water bodies.

limitations: Varies with leaf internal structure and canopy dry matter
Band wavelength shifts between 1.24 µm and 1.6 µm change dynamic range
science_references: Gao, B. C. (1996). NDWI—A normalized difference water index for remote sensing of vegetation liquid water from space. Remote Sensing of Environment, 58(3), 257-266.

typical_observed_range.context: Water > 0; built-up surfaces and soil yield distinct negative values

interpretation.caution: Replaces NIR with SWIR1 to suppress urban/built-up confusion found in McFeeters NDWI.

limitations: Shadows in high-relief or urban skyscraper canyons can still mimic water
science_references: Xu, H. (2006). Modification of normalised difference water index (NDWI) to enhance open water features in remotely sensed imagery. International Journal of Remote Sensing, 27(14), 3025-3033.

typical_observed_range.context: Healthy vegetation high positive; burned areas strongly negative

limitations: Single-date NBR cannot separate low productivity or bare soil from burned areas without pre-fire baseline
science_references: Key, C. H., & Benson, N. C. (2006). Landscape Assessment (LA): Sampling and Analysis Methods. USDA Forest Service General Technical Report RMRS-GTR-164-CD.

indices.name_ar: مؤشر تغير شدة الحريق المعياري (الفرق قبل وبعد الحريق)

mathematical_range.conditions: Standard difference range; multiply by 1000 if using USGS scaled convention.

typical_observed_range.context: Unburned: -0.1 to 0.1; Low severity: 0.1 to 0.27; High severity: > 0.66 (unscaled)

interpretation.caution: USGS burn severity classes (e.g., 0.10, 0.27, 0.44, 0.66) are reference guidelines for US ecosystems. Always specify whether values are unitless (-1 to 1) or scaled by 1000 (-1000 to 1000).

limitations: Requires pre- and post-fire seasonal alignment to prevent phenology bias
Phenological green-up or snow alters difference values
science_references: Key, C. H., & Benson, N. C. (2006). Landscape Assessment (LA): Sampling and Analysis Methods. USDA Forest Service General Technical Report RMRS-GTR-164-CD.

interpretation.caution: Severe confusion with bare dry soil and rocky outcrops. Never classify built-up solely on NDBI > 0.

limitations: High false positive rate over arid, semi-arid, and fallow agricultural soil
science_references: Zha, Y., et al. (2003). Use of normalized difference built-up index in automatically mapping urban areas from TM imagery. International Journal of Remote Sensing, 24(3), 583-594.

typical_observed_range.context: Bare soil yields positive values; dense vegetation yields negative

limitations: May overlap with dry non-photosynthetic vegetation
science_references: Rikimaru, A., et al. (2002). Tropical forest cover density mapping. ITTO Tropical Forest Update, 12(2), 9-11.

typical_observed_range.context: Snow typically > 0.4; water can overlap unless NIR threshold is applied

interpretation.caution: NDSI shares identical formula with MNDWI (Green-SWIR1). Context and NIR brightness (e.g. NIR > 0.11) are required to separate snow from water.

limitations: Requires cloud masking: cirrus and ice clouds show high NDSI values
Deep mountain shadows distort snow extraction
science_references: Hall, D. K., et al. (1995). Mapping snow cover with MODIS Airborne Simulator data. Remote Sensing of Environment, 54(2), 127-140.

mathematical_range.conditions: Requires red-edge band (Sentinel-2, RapidEye, PlanetScope SuperDove, WorldView-3).

typical_observed_range.context: Sensitive to chlorophyll in dense crops where standard NDVI saturates

limitations: Not available on standard 4-band sensors (Landsat 4-8, older satellites)
science_references: Barnes, E. M., et al. (2000). Coincident detection of crop water stress, nitrogen status and canopy density using ground-based multispectral data. In Proceedings of the 5th International Conference on Precision Agriculture.

mathematical_range.conditions: Valid over water bodies; requires accurate atmospheric water-surface correction.

typical_observed_range.context: Higher values indicate elevated chlorophyll-a and potential algal blooms

interpretation.caution: NDCI is a relative optical proxy; converting to physical chlorophyll-a concentration (mg/m³) requires local in-situ calibration and atmospheric correction for inland waters (e.g. C2RCC/ACOLITE).

limitations: Inaccurate over land or cloud shadows; must be masked to water bodies first
Sensitive to suspended sediment and CDOM
science_references: Mishra, S., & Mishra, D. R. (2012). Normalized difference chlorophyll index: A novel model for remote estimation of chlorophyll-a in turbid productive waters. Remote Sensing of Environment, 117, 394-406.

required_inputs.description: VV backscatter power in LINEAR units (NOT decibels dB!)
VH cross-polarization power in LINEAR units

mathematical_range.conditions: Inputs MUST be linear power (intensity = 10^(dB/10)), never raw dB.

typical_observed_range.context: Bare surface / smooth water ~ 0; dense rough canopy ~ 0.5 - 0.7

interpretation.caution: Radar RVI measures volumetric microwave scattering, NOT optical greenness. Distinct from Jordan 1969 optical Ratio Vegetation Index.

limitations: Sensitive to soil roughness, dielectric moisture, and incidence angle
Speckle filtering is mandatory before index calculation
science_references: Charbonneau, F. J., et al. (2005). Evaluation of Radarsat-2 polarimetric capabilities for crop monitoring. In Proceedings of the 5th International Symposium on Retrieval of Bio-and Geophysical Parameters from SAR Data.

indices.name_en: Ratio Vegetation Index (Jordan 1969 - Optical Simple Ratio)

mathematical_range.conditions: Non-negative inputs. In dense green canopy, value can exceed 10.0.

interpretation.caution: Do NOT confuse with Radar Vegetation Index. This is the classic 1969 optical simple ratio.

limitations: Highly sensitive to low RED values; approaches infinity as RED approaches zero
science_references: Jordan, C. F. (1969). Derivation of leaf-area index from quality of light on the forest floor. Ecology, 50(4), 663-666.
